q: On which appliance's energy label is the Energy Efficiency Factor (EEF) shown?
n: On the Philippine energy label, refrigerators are rated by Energy Efficiency Factor (EEF) and air conditioners by EER or CSPF. Source: DOE (Philippines) Philippine Energy Labeling Program.

q: What is the maximum number of outlets usually allowed on a 15-amp circuit?
n: Each general outlet is counted at 180 VA. A 15 A × 230 V circuit (3,450 VA) at 80% loading carries about 2,760 VA, roughly 10–15 outlets, and 10 is the common design rule. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (branch circuit loads).

q: What is a flat silicon cell that turns sunlight into electricity?
n: A photovoltaic (PV) cell is a flat silicon semiconductor that converts sunlight directly into electricity. Source: IEC 61215 (PV modules); US DOE Solar Energy Technologies Office.

q: What do you call an enclosure or location used to house electrical or communication components, which may be surface-mounted or recessed?
n: A utility box is an enclosure, surface-mounted or recessed, that houses electrical or communication components such as devices and connections. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (boxes); wiring device catalogs.

q: Which is NOT a standard fluorescent lamp wattage?
n: Linear fluorescent tubes come in standard wattages such as 18/20 W, 36/40 W and 58 W. 100 W is not a standard tube wattage. Source: IEC 60081 (double-capped fluorescent lamps).

q: To control one light from four locations, what switches are needed?
n: One light from four locations needs a 3-way switch at each end and a 4-way switch at each intermediate location: two 3-way switches and two 4-way switches. Source: Philippine Electrical Code; standard wiring diagrams.

q: What is the recommended spotlight angle for highlighting walls or paintings?
n: A narrow beam of about 20–30° concentrates light on paintings and wall features without spilling over the whole wall. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (accent lighting).

q: Which switch has a pilot light so it can be found in the dark?
n: An illuminated switch has a small pilot light that glows when the switch is off, so it can be found in the dark. Source: Wiring device manufacturer literature.

q: What type of lighting is most suitable for a two-storey residential house?
n: Warm light (about 2,700–3,000 K) is preferred in houses for a relaxed, comfortable atmosphere. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (residential lighting).

q: What lighting emphasizes a specific area or object for drama?
n: Accent lighting focuses on a specific area or object to create drama and a focal point. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: What lighting suits a curved or wavy ceiling?
o: Indirect lighting at the base of the curve
n: Indirect light (uplighting) placed at the base of the curve washes up the curved or wavy ceiling and reveals its form. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: What lighting is used for reading at night?
n: Reading at night needs task lighting: localized light on the page at higher illuminance. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (recommended illuminances).

q: What lighting suits a reading desk?
n: A reading desk needs task lighting, such as a desk lamp, focused on the work surface. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: What lighting draws attention to an object or casts decorative patterns on a surface?
n: Accent lighting is directional and draws attention to an object or casts decorative patterns on a surface. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which of these saves up to about 75–80% energy compared with incandescent and gives bright light?
n: CFLs use about 20–25% of the power of incandescent lamps for the same light, saving about 75–80% of energy. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, Lighting Choices; DOE (Philippines) lighting programs.

q: Which type of light is best suited for outdoor parking areas?
n: High-intensity discharge lamps (metal halide, high-pressure sodium) give high output and efficacy over wide areas, suiting outdoor parking. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (parking facilities).

q: What type of lighting is ideal for a production area with a soffit on a suspended slab?
n: Troffers are recessed modular fixtures that fit into the soffit or ceiling grid under a suspended slab, giving even, glare-controlled light in production areas. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Why are downlights or pin lights commonly used in retail stores?
o: To emphasize the texture of materials
To preserve the original tone and color of materials
n: Downlights with high color rendering render merchandise in its true tone and color, which matters in retail. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (retail lighting).

q: What focuses or intensifies the direction of light?
n: A reflector redirects and concentrates light into a controlled beam. Diffusers spread it. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (luminaire optics).

q: What is the best type of lighting for a factory, considering its impact on the work environment?
n: Daylight-white light (about 5,000–6,500 K) supports alertness and clear visibility, suiting factory production work. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (industrial lighting).

q: What light color is generally preferred in offices for alertness?
n: Offices generally prefer cooler, daylight-colored light (about 4,000–6,500 K) for alertness and visual acuity. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (office lighting).

q: What does a diffuser in a luminaire do?
n: A diffuser scatters light from the lamps, softening it, spreading it evenly and reducing glare. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which type of lighting is best for directing and concentrating light to enhance visibility and mimic natural brightness?
n: Daylight-colored light most closely mimics natural brightness and enhances visibility. The other choices are luminaire parts, not lighting types. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which lamp has a filament?
n: An incandescent lamp produces light by heating a tungsten filament. LEDs and fluorescents have none. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Modular cubicles are installed in an office. How many electrical outlets per cubicle are recommended if the office uses a UPS system?
n: Two outlets per cubicle is recommended: one on the UPS circuit for computers and one regular outlet for other loads. Source: Office electrical design practice; Philippine Electrical Code.

q: Which lamp is efficient and long-lived but has no filament?
n: LEDs are solid-state semiconductor sources with no filament, giving high efficacy and long life. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: In office electrical systems, UPS stands for:
n: UPS = Uninterruptible Power Supply. A UPS uses batteries to keep computers and critical loads running through power interruptions, long enough to ride through or shut down safely. Source: IEC 62040.

q: What voltage serves general-purpose office outlets in the Philippines?
n: General-purpose outlets in the Philippines are 230 V nominal (commonly called 220 V), 60 Hz. Source: Philippine Grid Code; Meralco service standards.

q: What is used to start a fluorescent lamp?
n: In a preheat fluorescent circuit, the starter preheats the electrodes and then opens, letting the ballast strike the arc. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (fluorescent lamp circuits).

q: What starts and runs a compact fluorescent lamp?
n: A compact fluorescent lamp is started and run by an electronic ballast, usually built into the lamp base. Source: IES Lighting Handbook; IEC 61347.

q: What powers and controls an LED lamp?
n: An LED is powered and controlled by a driver, which supplies regulated DC current. Source: IES Lighting Handbook; IEC 61347-2-13.

q: What light is best for reading and writing?
n: Daylight-colored light gives high visual clarity for reading and writing. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: What type of switch is used to control a light from two different locations?
n: Two 3-way switches control one light from two locations, such as the ends of a hall. Source: Philippine Electrical Code; standard wiring diagrams.

q: Which is not a good location for light switches?
o: Beside the door on the direction of the swing
n: A switch behind the door is hidden when the door is open and hard to reach, so it is a poor location. Switches go on the latch side of the door. Source: Time-Saver Standards (residential electrical); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What type of switch is commonly used for staircases?
n: Stair lighting is controlled from top and bottom with a pair of three-way switches. Source: Philippine Electrical Code; standard wiring diagrams.

q: Before the widespread use of LED lighting, where was it originally used?
n: Early LEDs were dim and used as indicators. Before replacing general lighting, white LEDs were widely used first in flashlights and other portable lights. Source: US DOE Solid-State Lighting program history.

q: What is one disadvantage of LED lighting?
n: LEDs cost more up front than other lamps, though their efficiency and long life usually repay this. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, LED Lighting.

q: What commonly replaces older lamps in street lighting?
n: LED street lights are replacing high-pressure sodium and mercury vapor lamps because of their efficiency, long life and good optical control. Source: US DOE Solid-State Lighting (street lighting); DPWH lighting programs.
